request_billing.source: Tariff: the characters of the text the worker hands to ElevenLabs -- every text frame on the multi-stream WebSocket (text-to-speech and text-to-dialogue) and every chunked HTTP body -- counted as Unicode code points. Measured 2026-10-20 against api.elevenlabs.io with the account's credit counter and the HTTP character-cost header: a text-to-speech WebSocket generation is billed with its surrounding whitespace trimmed (a context's initial space, a sentence's trailing space and leading spaces are not billed; the plugin flushes each sentence frame as its own generation), while a text-to-dialogue WebSocket input and an HTTP body are billed whole, whitespace included. A completed request is charged its characters; a context closed at its first audio chunk (a barge-in), a context closed before it was flushed, and an HTTP response closed after its first chunk are each charged every character already handed; a 404 refusal is charged nothing. ElevenLabs documents no rule for an error or a failed connection (elevenlabs.io/docs/websockets, read 2026-10-20), so a request it refuses and one that ends in a connection or timeout failure are not charged: when the provider's rule is undocumented the customer gets the benefit of the doubt.

Tariff: Gemini's own cumulative usage report for the request -- prompt_token_count and the generated-audio candidates_token_count -- which the 3.x TTS models send on every streamed chunk and 2.5 with its single response chunk (measured 2026-10-20). A completed request is charged its latest valid report. A request the worker abandons mid-stream (a barge-in) is charged the latest report received before it stopped reading: Google documents no rule for an abandoned request, so Skysay bills what the provider itself reported up to that moment and never an estimate. A request Gemini refuses is not charged: 'If your request fails with a 400 or 500 error, you won't be charged for the tokens used' (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing, read 2026-10-20); nor is one that ends in a connection or timeout failure, whose usage cannot be established. A request that never produced audio -- Gemini's answer without audio, or one the worker cancelled before its first audio -- is treated as Gemini's refusal and not charged.

billing.provider_price_basis: Soniox real-time STT is priced at $2/M input-audio tokens and $4/M output-text tokens; 500 input-audio plus 250 output-text tokens/minute are the provider's public usage references observed 2026-08-22. Pinned managed retail is 1.5x those token rates.

Soniox real-time TTS is priced at $4/M input-text tokens and $21.50/M output-audio tokens; 250 input-text plus 500 output-audio tokens/minute are the provider's public usage references observed 2026-08-22. Pinned managed retail is 1.25x each token rate, rounded up to whole micro-USD.
Fish Audio paid S2 Pro public list price $15/M UTF-8 bytes observed 2026-08-22; retail is 1.25x rounded up.

request_billing.source: Tariff: the UTF-8 bytes of the text frames the worker hands to Fish Audio's connection; Fish bills TTS on the size of the input text (docs.fish.audio/developer-guide/models-pricing/pricing-and-rate-limits, read 2026-10-20). A completed request and one the worker cancels are charged those bytes. Fish documents no TTS error or cancellation rule (it does document that errored ASR requests are not billed), so a request Fish refuses with a finish error, and one that ends in a connection or timeout failure, is not charged: when the provider's rule is undocumented the customer gets the benefit of the doubt.

billing.provider_price_basis: Cartesia standard TTS is approximately one credit per submitted character; Cartesia's public Pro overage price was $65 per million credits when read 2026-08-29. Pinned managed retail is 1.25x that public overage rate, rounded up to whole micro-USD per character. The reserve uses Cartesia's published 750-800 credits per minute range conservatively at 800.

request_billing.source: Tariff: the transcript characters the worker hands to Cartesia's connection. A completed request and one the worker cancels (barge-in, teardown, its own deadline) are charged those characters: Cartesia's contexts guide (docs.cartesia.ai/use-the-api/tts-websocket/contexts, read 2026-10-20) says a cancel only halts generations that have not begun, and the plugin sends each sentence with max_buffer_delay_ms 0, so a handed sentence is generated. A request Cartesia refuses with an error is not charged: 'errors will not consume credits' (docs.cartesia.ai/pricing, read 2026-10-20). A request that ends in a connection or timeout failure is not charged, because its delivery cannot be established.

billing.provider_price_basis: Azure AI Speech standard (S1) real-time speech to text lists at $1.00 per audio hour -- meter 'S1 Speech To Text', Azure Retail Prices API (https://prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices), the same figure in germanywestcentral, eastus and southeastasia, read 2026-08-30 -- which is 277.78 micro-USD per audio second. Pinned managed retail is 1.25x that, rounded up to whole micro-USD. The reserve is one audio second per second of call, as for Google Chirp 2. Continuous language identification does not change this: the same audio-hour meter is the only real-time transcription meter the retail catalogue publishes for this region (1580 AI + Machine Learning price rows read 2026-09-01, no identification meter among them), and the adapter reports the same audio-second usage whether it listens for one language or three.

Azure AI Speech standard (S1) prebuilt neural text to speech lists at $15.00 per 1M characters -- meter 'S1 Neural Text To Speech Characters', Azure Retail Prices API (https://prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices), the same figure in germanywestcentral, eastus and southeastasia, read 2026-08-30 -- i.e. 15 micro-USD per character. Pinned managed retail is 1.25x that, rounded up to whole micro-USD. The 900-character reserve is the same per-minute speaking estimate the ElevenLabs rows use. Microsoft's billable character count is NOT the submitted length: CJK characters count double and some SSML markup is billable, so the worker meters with its own counter rather than LiveKit's.

request_billing.source: Tariff: Microsoft's billable characters of the escaped SSML text the worker hands to the connection when it writes the request body. Microsoft bills 'each successfully processed request', regardless of whether audio output is produced (learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-services/speech-service/text-to-speech, Pricing note, read 2026-10-20), so a completed request and one the worker cancels after writing it are charged; a request Microsoft refuses (HTTP 4xx/5xx) is not charged, nor one that ends in a connection or timeout failure, whose processing cannot be established.

billing.provider_price_basis: OpenAI GPT-Live Transcribe lists at $0.017 per audio minute (283.333 micro-USD per second), observed 2026-10-20 at https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-live-transcribe and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing. Pinned managed retail rounds up to 284 micro-USD per provider-reported audio second. Finite workflow listener only; ordinary cascade transport is not qualified.

live_sources.basis: Founder ruling 2026-10-21: GPT-Live-1 is a speech-to-speech model whose provider publishes no per-language list for it, so it declares every language and none is blocked up front; the risk is taken deliberately. A managed named list is a possible later step. Which languages Skysay has tested is the functional record, not this row.

workflow_source_measurement.source: Deepgram bills streamed audio and its stream never states the billed seconds. A workflow listener is charged the PCM seconds the worker wrote to the open Deepgram connection (samples sent / 24000); queued frames never sent, keep-alives and CloseStream are not audio. Settled as measured_partial evidence at the row's audio-second rate.

Azure real-time speech to text bills audio hours and the recognizer never states them. A workflow listener is charged the PCM seconds the Azure SDK push stream accepted in the worker's isolated recognizer process (native 16 kHz samples counted at each successful write, acknowledged after the session started / 16000). Settled as measured_partial evidence at the row's audio-second rate.

Soniox bills real-time STT in tokens that only its usage log states. A workflow listener is charged the PCM seconds the worker wrote to the open Soniox connection (samples sent / 24000), converted at the provider's public per-minute usage references the reserve already uses (500 input-audio and 250 output-text tokens per minute), rounded down per dimension. Settled as measured_partial evidence.

Soniox bills real-time TTS in tokens that only its usage log states. A workflow authored line is charged the PCM seconds the provider returned for its request (samples received / 24000), converted at the provider's public per-minute usage references the reserve already uses (250 input-text and 500 output-audio tokens per minute), rounded down per dimension. Settled as measured_partial evidence.

A GPT-Live workflow line is spoken by the call's live session, which states no per-line duration. It is charged the seconds of that line's speech the session played out to the caller (the SDK's playback position of each segment that finished while the line held the session), at the GPT-Live duration rate. Settled as measured_partial evidence.
